restated: For every P-position (p,q,r) of 3-row Chomp with r >= 1, p - q <= 3r - 1. Equivalently, for each fixed r, f(q,r) - q is at most 3r - 1 for every q >= r.
ledger_statement: CORRECTION of C0009 and (Z1). Byrnes' Lemma 5, correctly specialised to 3-row Chomp with the third row fixed, gives p - q <= 3r - 1 for EVERY P-position (p,q,r), uniformly in q. The embedding forced by Byrnes' assumption (1) is C = the row-2 tail, D = the row-1 tail, A = the 3r-1 cells of columns 1..r minus the poison, giving m = q-r and n = p-r. C0009 used n = p-q, which yields the weaker true statement (p-q)-(q-r) <= 3r-1 and a spurious (q-r) term that appears to grow with q. Consequence: (Z1) is NOT half-proved, it is fully proved in print with C = 3, and M_r <= 3r-2. The 'residual half of (Z1)' that the Phase 0 audit set as island 01's opening target does not exist.

verdicts.first_gap_line: The outcome A_{m,n} = ( row1 = r+n, row2 = r+min(m,n), row3 = r ), that is, taking n >= m so that p >= q, m = q - r and n = p - r.
verdicts.gap_description: After removing {x : x >= d_{n+1}} with d_{n+1} = (1, r+n+1) under the componentwise order, row 2 is truncated to min(r+m, r+n) only in the inequality-coordinate sense; Chomp's upper set of (1, r+n+1) in this 3-row board must also delete (3, j) for every j >= r+n+1. So the row-3 length of A_{m,n} is r only when r <= r+n, which requires n >= 0, and the claimed exact identification with (p,q,r) is not established. Consequently the assertion that every P-position (p,q,r) is some A_{m,n} with m = q-r and n = p-r is unproven: there is no specialization, only the weaker conditional bound (p-q)-(q-r) <= 3r-1 at the diagonal q=r.

verdicts.effectivity_check: No effective new constant is produced. The proof does not attempt to bound N(r) or the period, and the only bound obtained at the valid specialization is f(r,r) <= 4r-1, with the claimed y=3r-1 uniform-in-q bound dependent on a coordinate identification that fails.

verdicts.first_gap_line: reading `n` as `p - q` instead of `p - r` yields `(p-q) - (q-r) <= 3r - 1` ... but it is not what Lemma 5 gives ... Under the correct coordinate there is nothing left to prove.
verdicts.gap_description: Byrnes' setup has A, C, D pairwise disjoint in X, so truncation at c_{m+1} and d_{n+1} can only remove outright the elements of the two tails C and D chosen for n and m; the remaining chain elements c_1..c_m and d_1..d_n are are NOT cells of Chomp positions, differing from the claimed surrogates c_j=(2,r+j), d_j=(1,r+j). For the claimed surrogates the row-2 tail is not a chain under the componentwise order (incomparability and non-transitivity), and deleting {x >= d_{n+1}} necessarily removes (2,r+1..r+n) as well, producing (r+n, r+min(m,n), r), so the generic Byrnes position A_{m,n} is not the Chomp position (p,q,r). In the only genuinely-by-Byrnes embedding (Byrnes' one-chain Corollary 4 with the second row as the chain and the first and third rows fixed in A, D adjoined), the coordinates force n=p-q, m=q-r, and Lemma 5's unconditional clause delivers only (p-q)-(q-r) = f(q,r)-2q+r <= 3r-1; for q>r the appended negative coefficient -2q is not valid for the quantity f(q,r)-q that the claim seeks to bound. Since the claim's bound is entirely unsupported, the proof has a fatal logical gap regardless of the unlimited numerical agreement.
